summary.oneLiner: Sapphire Foods India Limited is one of Yum! Brands' largest franchisees in India and Sri Lanka, operating KFC, Pizza Hut and Taco Bell restaurants across the subcontinent.
summary.business: Sapphire Foods operates quick-service restaurants (QSR) under the KFC, Pizza Hut and Taco Bell brands as a franchisee of Yum! Brands Inc., running 1,052 restaurants (916 in India, 136 in Sri Lanka) as of 31 March 2026. The company is principally promoted by Sapphire Foods Mauritius Limited, backed by private-equity investors, with a long-term ownership lock-in of 25.1% of equity under an arrangement with Yum!.

currentContext.strengths: One of Yum! Brands' largest franchise partners in India and Sri Lanka, operating three of the largest and fastest-growing QSR brands (KFC, Pizza Hut, Taco Bell) across the subcontinent|Recognised as 'World's Best KFC Franchisee' and among the 'World's Top 4 Pizza Hut Franchisees' at the Yum! Global Franchise Convention (April 2025), indicating strong execution relative to peer franchisees|Exclusive Pizza Hut territory in Tamil Nadu delivers a proven dine-in-forward omni-channel template with double-digit delta in SSSG and restaurant EBITDA margin versus the rest of the network|#1 QSR brand position in Sri Lanka, with the Sri Lanka business delivering double-digit SSSG for two consecutive years|Technology-led efficiency: despite multi-fold growth in financial transaction volumes since 2018, digitisation and automation have let the company cut finance team headcount by 25% versus 2018|Strong people/culture moat: mean Gallup Engagement Score rose from 4.12 (FY2018) to 4.52 (FY2025), global percentile rank rose from 57 to 81, and the company won the Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award for a 6th consecutive year (one of only 4 Indian companies recognised in 2026)|Ranked No.1 in DJSI ESG score among QSRs in India and No.3 among global QSRs
currentContext.strategies: Expand consumer penetration by attracting new users rather than relying solely on increasing consumption frequency — building awareness among non-users, strengthening consideration, and delivering a differentiated product, service and value experience.|At KFC, pursue a two-pronged marketing and value-led strategy tailored separately to 'Evolving' chicken-consuming markets (North & West) and 'More-Developed' chicken-consuming markets (South, e.g. Tamil Nadu) to drive Dine-In and Takeaway transactions and grow the consumer base.|At Pizza Hut, replicate the Tamil Nadu blueprint — an exclusive-territory, dine-in-forward omni-channel template backed by superior product innovation and consistent, ahead-of-curve brand marketing investment — across other markets to shift consumer perceptions and gain market share as the No.2 QSR pizza brand.|Calibrate the pace of new restaurant additions using an internal operating principle that benchmarks individual and cohort-level restaurant payback performance, dialling expansion up or down rather than growing unconditionally.|Pursue the proposed merger with Devyani International to unify a go-to-market model that previously required alignment between two franchisees and a global brand owner, aiming to create the largest restaurant operator in India with sharper franchisee-level execution rights and faster decision-making.|Continue deploying technology and automation (beyond finance, already delivering headcount efficiency) into new-restaurant-opening management, logistics management, and menu/recipe management tied to revenue assurance, to improve organisation-wide efficiency and accuracy.|Operate on five core principles — passion for food and the brands served, execution excellence, disciplined capital allocation, capability/capital to operate a multi-brand (KFC, Pizza Hut, Taco Bell) platform, and values-based culture and governance.|The Board has not recommended any dividend for FY2025-26; the Company has not transferred any amount to the general reserves, to the Investor Education & Protection Fund, or to an Unpaid Dividend Account. Dividend decisions are governed by a Board-adopted Dividend Distribution Policy based on parameters specified under the SEBI Listing Regulations, available on the Company's website.
currentContext.expansion: Sapphire Foods added 89 new restaurants in FY26 (73 KFC, 7 Pizza Hut in India, 9 in Sri Lanka), taking the total network to 1,052 restaurants (916 in India, 136 in Sri Lanka) across KFC, Pizza Hut and Taco Bell. KFC's total store count rose from 502 (FY25) to 575 (FY26), spreading across 156 cities (up from 131), with the brand's stated priority to continue its current pace of expansion at 60-80 stores per year, while calibrating additions against restaurant-level payback economics — CY25 net additions were dialled down to 60 stores, largely in existing markets. Pizza Hut's expansion remained cautious using a smaller ~1,000-1,200 sq ft store format, with zero store additions in CY25 and 7 in FY26 (total store count reaching 341 across 82 cities), as the company prioritised restoring store-level profitability before deploying further capital. Sri Lanka added 9 new restaurants during the year, taking its network to 136 restaurants (up 7% YoY) across 77 cities, maintaining the #1 QSR brand position in the country. Digital Kiosks have been rolled out across 73% of the KFC restaurant estate as part of a frictionless-customer-experience initiative, and the company continues capital expenditure on sustainability projects such as rooftop solar installation and IGBC-aligned upgrades to make restaurants greener where feasible.
currentContext.mdna: India's QSR & cloud-kitchen market is large (~Rs.499 Bn in 2023) and growing at ~17% CAGR toward an estimated Rs.1,516 Bn by 2030, with the organized share of foodservice projected to rise from 45% to 50% and QSR/cloud-kitchen's share of that organized market from 21% to 28%.|Chicken and Pizza cuisines together represent ~32% of the QSR market and are growing at roughly 1.5x the pace of other cuisines, underpinning the long-term opportunity for KFC and Pizza Hut.|Consumer demand has remained structurally weak, with private final consumption expenditure (PFCE) lagging GDP growth, and competitive intensity has risen due to democratised distribution networks and easier access to investment capital for new entrant brands — pressuring same-store sales growth industry-wide.|Delivery continues to grow as a share of restaurant sales across KFC, Pizza Hut and the Sri Lanka business, reflecting an ongoing channel mix shift.|Sri Lanka's macroeconomic recovery (2025 real GDP growth estimated at 5%, following the 2022 crisis), supported by macro stabilisation and structural reforms, underpins continued momentum in that market.|India's economy remains resilient and among the fastest-growing globally (7.7% real GDP growth estimated for FY 2025-26), with per-capita disposable income rising, providing a supportive medium-term backdrop for QSR consumption despite near-term softness in discretionary spending.

risks.note: Changes in industry, economic and geo-political factors, including global events, can affect the availability and cost of key inputs, the cost of operations, and business continuity. Management mitigates this through collaboration with YUM! Brands to assess industry/economic factors, proactive tracking of commodity prices and supply-chain developments, supply-chain planning with buffer stock, alternate sourcing, and driving sales/value proposition to maintain competitiveness.

Exposure to breakdown of or unauthorised access to IT systems and threats from virus attacks/hacking. Mitigated through secured IT policies and processes, regular upgrades, investment in Next-Gen Security Tools, and continuous monitoring to prevent/remediate breaches.

The Company must comply with continuously evolving regulations across Food Safety, Employment and Labour, Taxation, Environment, and Health and Safety; failure to comply could result in penalties, reputational damage or criminal prosecution. Mitigated through a compliance management framework, an in-house digitised regulatory compliance platform, regular training on food-safety and other regulations, and periodic food-safety/quality assessments across restaurants, supply-chain centres and vendors.

Includes business impact from sales variations, delayed paybacks on new restaurants, disruption in the supply chain, high attrition of restaurant staff, and other business uncertainties. Mitigated through robust business-plan evaluation and monitoring, data-driven site selection for new restaurants, an improved-payback compact omni-channel format, marketing collaboration with YUM! to build brand awareness and counter competitor actions, strengthened supply-chain/distribution systems, strategic resource planning and hiring, and business-continuity-planning (BCP) processes.

one-line thesis: Sapphire Foods delivered its strongest quarter in 3 years with KFC SSSG hitting 6% (ex-calendar) driven by a permanent INR99 value layer and behavior-changing advertising, validating the turnaround strategy just as the complex merger with Devyani International enters the final regulatory approval phase. While Pizza Hut India remains challenged, the Sri Lanka business continues to defy macro volatility with double-digit growth, positioning the combined entity for dominant market share post-merger.
financial scorecard: Revenue INR7.9bn (+11% YoY); Consolidated Adj EBITDA INR61cr (+20% YoY, 7.7% margin); PAT reported negative INR15.5cr (impacted by INR6.2cr Labour Code one-off & INR6.6cr merger/ESOP costs); Normalized PBT positive INR8cr; No order book (retail model); Net debt not explicitly quantified but capex heavy at INR320cr for the year.
guidance: FY27 Capex expected to match FY26 levels (~INR320cr); KFC SSSG trajectory targeting mid-single digits sustained by new strategy; No immediate price hikes planned unless raw material/oil costs spike dramatically; Merger completion expected by end of FY27 (12-15 month process from Jan 2026 announcement).
order book & pipeline: N/A - Retail restaurant model; Store expansion pipeline includes 73 KFC openings in FY26 (total 575) and 9 Sri Lanka openings; FY27 capex guided similar to FY26 driven by new stores, refurbishments, and renewal fees.
segment / subsidiary detail: KFC India: Revenue +15%, SSSG +4% (+6% ex-Navratri), Rest EBITDA margin 16.8% (+110bps QoQ); Pizza Hut India: Revenue -6%, SSSG -7%, Rest EBITDA margin -3.3%; Sri Lanka: Revenue +15% LKR, SSSG +11%, Rest EBITDA margin 14.6% (pressed by minimum wage hikes).
growth verticals / optionality: Merger with Devyani International to create unified largest QSR player in India; Sri Lanka expansion accelerating (9 stores in FY26, highest in 3 years) with potential for high single/low double digit additions next 2-3 years; Digital kiosk rollout (73% complete) driving APC uplift.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin supported by vendor partnerships on value meals; Risk of 50-70bps GM pressure if vendor support withdraws; LPG inflation impacting EBITDA by 30-50bps; Marketing spend increased by 75-100bps to drive recruitment; Minimum wage hikes in Sri Lanka offset operating leverage.
capex / expansion: INR320cr in FY26 comprising new store openings (KFC ~INR2.1-2.2cr/store, PH ~INR1.35-1.4cr/store), 5/10-year refurbishments, and franchise renewal fees kicking in after 10 years.
capital allocation: Priority on organic store expansion and refurbishments; Merger-related costs (INR6.6cr) incurred for employee retention/ESOP modification; No dividend commentary; Focus on deleveraging via EBITDA growth.
risks & watch-items: LPG availability and pricing volatility (25-40% cost increase); Raw material inflation; Pizza Hut India structural underperformance; Merger execution risk (NCLT/SEBI/CCI approvals pending 7-10 months); Sri Lanka macro/geopolitical instability.
management quality / tone: Highly confident on KFC strategy validation ('finally got it right'); Cautiously optimistic on consumer demand despite peer caution; Transparent on one-offs; Pragmatic on inflation pass-through; Long-term focused on merger synergies.
non-obvious takeaways: Vendor partners are cross-subsidizing the INR99 value meal (fries/beverage suppliers) to gain volume, masking true gross margin impact which could emerge later; The 'renewal fee' component of capex is a hidden structural cost increase as the franchise matures past 10 years; KFC's own delivery app is outperforming aggregators significantly, reducing commission drag over time.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Margin pressure from LPG inflation and heavy marketing spend; Pizza Hut drag | Devyani International | beneficiary | High | Merger creates scale to absorb costs, unify supply chain, and dominate QSR market; Sapphire's KFC turnaround de-risks the combined entity's largest revenue pillar. |
| Vendor margin compression due to cross-subsidization of value meals | Varun Beverages Ltd | loser | Med | As a key beverage partner mentioned in vendor support, may face volume-for-margin trade-offs if value meal mix skews heavily towards subsidized bundles. |

themes.title: QSR & organized foodservice
themes.need: QSR/foodservice operators are driven by store-count, SSSG and unit-economics/ADS recovery - dine-in/delivery operating leverage, distinct from grocery quick-commerce and apparel-format retail.
themes.driver: Store-count adds + SSSG/ADS recovery and dine-in/delivery operating leverage.
